assignment: Numerical PDE finite differences and finite volumes: elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic schemes; consistency, stability, convergence, exact Lax equivalence hypotheses, CFL, monotone scalar conservation laws and entropy limits, numerical fluxes, splitting, discrete energy, and boundary conditions.
method: Public author or university course PDFs were downloaded into ignored scratchpad storage and extracted with Python 3 / PyMuPDF (fitz). The page ranges below distinguish complete PDFs/chapters from selected notes. Source text, not a search-result snippet, was read for every claim marked used.

sources.citation: Endre Süli, B6.1 Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations: A brief introduction to the theory of finite difference approximation of partial differential equations, Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford, 10 November 2025.
sources.acquisition_note: Public full lecture-note PDF from the author's Oxford University page. The 110-page PDF was extracted and read in full, including the contents, all proofs and the final nonlinear finite-difference discussion.

units.anchor: Entire note, Sections 1–6.7, including function-space and elliptic prerequisites, linear finite-difference schemes, heat and wave equations, first-order hyperbolic equations, and the closing scalar nonlinear scheme discussion
claims_used: discrete grid norms and finite-difference operators
interior and boundary consistency plus stability as the error proof for linear elliptic boundary difference schemes
discrete summation by parts, discrete Poincare and energy/max-norm arguments for elliptic schemes
heat theta schemes, Fourier stability, CFL thresholds and the difference between L2 stability and a discrete maximum principle
wave energy estimates and the one-dimensional explicit wave CFL bound
first-order hyperbolic inflow boundaries, upwind schemes and energy estimates
the note's final pointwise upwind estimate for a smooth scalar nonlinear solution and its explicit refusal to cover weak/discontinuous solutions
limits: The nonlinear discussion at pp. 108–110 is a pointwise smooth-solution L-infinity estimate only; it does not prove convergence to an entropy solution across shocks.
The abstract consistency-plus-stability theorem in §3 is for an elliptic boundary-value scheme; it is not the Lax–Richtmyer initial-value equivalence theorem.
The Bramble–Hilbert lemma is cited for one rough-data error estimate rather than proved in this note.
The note is finite-difference focused and does not supply the nonlinear finite-volume entropy convergence theorem needed below.

sources.citation: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Finite Difference and Spectral Methods for Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations, unpublished author text (1996), Chapter 4: Accuracy, Stability, and Convergence.
sources.acquisition_note: Public author-hosted chapter PDF. The author resource page says the text is available for use without restriction except copies must not alter the original text and must include the author's name. Full chapter is cached only in ignored scratchpad; the dossier records citations and limitations, not a redistributed chapter.

units.anchor: Entire Chapter 4, §§4.1–4.8 as present in the author-hosted 40-page file: accuracy/stability/convergence, Lax equivalence, CFL, von Neumann analysis, pseudospetra/Kreiss matrix theorem, vector/multistep schemes and a method-of-lines section
units.pdf_pages_read: 1–40 (complete file; no pages omitted; the closing §4.7 explicitly says the section is not yet written)
claims_used: abstract Lax–Richtmyer setup: a well-posed linear IVP u_t=Au on a Banach space B, bounded linear one-step maps S_k on B, fixed mesh function h=h(k), and convergence/stability definitions in one common norm
consistency order p: for sufficiently smooth exact solutions, ||u(t+k)-S_k u(t)||=O(k^(p+1)); consistency means p>0
convergence: S_k^n u0 tends to the exact solution at fixed finite times as k tends to zero for every initial datum u0 in B
stability: ||S_k^n|| is uniformly bounded for all n,k with 0<=nk<=T, with the bound independent of k

Theorem 4.1 statement: for a consistent approximation to a well-posed linear IVP, convergence iff stability; the theorem allows multiple dimensions, implicit formulas, boundary conditions, space-variable coefficients, lower-order terms and vector/multistep formulas after one-step augmentation
CFL theorem: numerical domain of dependence must contain the mathematical domain of dependence; it is necessary for convergence and is not sufficient for stability
von Neumann scalar one-step criterion and the distinction between scalar amplification-factor tests and vector/multistep matrix-power estimates
non-normality can make eigenvalue/spectral-radius checks insufficient; resolvents/pseudospectra or power bounds are needed
bounded-time stability rather than long-time stability and mesh-family dependence
limits: The author explicitly labels §4.2 as sketchy and says essential rigor is omitted, especially the operator A being defined on a dense subspace rather than all of B and the relationship between continuous and discrete norms.

The Lax equivalence theorem proof and global accuracy theorem proof are explicitly marked 'Not yet written'; the chapter is a source for exact statement/hypothesis shape, not a complete proof supplier.
Several later proofs are likewise marked unwritten; §4.7 method-of-lines is explicitly not yet written. Do not claim that reading the complete file means every theorem in it has a complete proof.

The source's consistency notation uses a common Banach-space setting; a grid implementation needs explicit interpolation/embedding and norm-comparison hypotheses to transfer it to mesh-dependent spaces.

units.anchor: Entire note, especially §§1–2.6: transport, finite volume principles, scalar conservation-law schemes, monotone schemes and convergence
claims_used: cell-average finite-volume derivation
monotone consistent flux and CFL update
L-infinity and BV estimates
the compactness-to-entropy-limit proof for BV initial data
distinction between the detailed BV route and the later no-BV entropy-process/Young-measure route
limits: The no-BV route is summarized and referred to Eymard–Gallouët–Herbin, rather than proved in this note.
The BV route imports Helly compactness and entropy-solution uniqueness; neither is manufactured by the finite-volume argument itself.

sources.citation: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik Skre Fjordholm, and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical methods for conservation laws and related equations, ETH Zürich lecture notes, public course copy (2019 course materials).
sources.acquisition_note: Public ETH course-material PDF. The full file, including the detailed monotone finite-volume convergence proof and all nonblank pages, was extracted and read; empty separator pages were noted explicitly.

units.anchor: All chapters and appendix; Chapters 1–4 on scalar conservation laws and monotone schemes; Chapters 5–6 on high-resolution/ENO/WENO schemes; Chapters 7–9 on systems
claims_used: weak and entropy formulations
monotone scalar FV theorem and proof route
TVD/SSP and high-order reconstruction limitations
entropy pairs and local small-data Riemann solvers for systems
flux and entropy-flux formulations
limits: Theorem 4.19 assumes a uniform mesh-to-time ratio bound dt/dx >= c > 0 in addition to the CFL condition; it uses a piecewise-linear-in-time interpolant and BV initial data.
The proof cites Helly/BV compactness to Giusti; Appendix A contains only Gronwall, not a Helly proof.
The entropy PDE existence/uniqueness theory in Chapter 3 is sketched and refers to Holden–Risebro/GR91; it is not a complete local proof of Kruzhkov uniqueness.

The system Riemann solver is local for small data under strict hyperbolicity and each characteristic field genuinely nonlinear or linearly degenerate; no general large-data system convergence result is supplied.

existing_suppliers_checked.limit: These prove continuum scalar PDE facts. They do not state or prove monotonicity, entropy stability, CFL, or convergence of a discrete finite-volume scheme.

claims_supplied: Poincare control and a priori energy estimates
existing_suppliers_checked.limit: They supply continuum elliptic analysis, not a discrete coercivity/stability estimate or a finite-difference error theorem.

claims_supplied: continuous heat maximum-principle and energy contexts
continuous wave energy identity, stability, and boundary flux cancellation
existing_suppliers_checked.limit: The numerical proof still must establish a discrete summation-by-parts identity, discrete boundary flux cancellation and any mesh-dependent CFL condition.

claims_supplied: Rellich compactness for bounded Sobolev sequences
Frechet–Kolmogorov compactness under boundedness, tail and translation hypotheses
existing_suppliers_checked.limit: The inventory has no checked Helly selection/BV compactness theorem and no discrete entropy compactness theorem; Rellich applies only after its Sobolev hypotheses are proved, which monotone FV convergence does not generally provide.

claims_supplied: pointwise bounded families of bounded linear maps on a Banach domain are uniformly bounded in operator norm
existing_suppliers_checked.limit: This supplies the functional-analysis step for the converse of abstract Lax equivalence once every discrete operator acts on one common Banach space and convergence is assumed for every datum. It does not supply the grid embeddings or mesh-dependent norm equivalence omitted by Trefethen's source proof.
The PDE plan explicitly marks numerical PDE out of scope (§3) and PDE-26 deliberately treats scalar conservation laws; it is a scope record, not a numerical theorem supplier.
